subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate or preempt compaction/memoryFlush from the foreground session lane, or treat the current foreground lane model with shorter timeouts and diagnostics as the intended behavior?
rationale: The source-backed failure remains, but the durable fix changes scheduler priority, session ordering, transcript safety, and recovery semantics across active user turns and background maintenance.

options.title: Isolate maintenance lane
options.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency maintenance lane or worker so foreground user messages can be admitted, acknowledged, or scheduled without waiting for the full maintenance timeout.

options.title: Make maintenance preemptible
options.body: Keep the current lane model but abort and reschedule compaction/memoryFlush when fresh user work arrives, trading simpler ownership for more abort/retry complexity.

options.title: Accept timeout mitigation
options.body: Keep active compaction/memoryFlush in the foreground session lane and rely on the 180-second default timeout plus stuck-session diagnostics as the product behavior.

recommendation.title: Isolate maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency maintenance lane or worker so foreground user messages can be admitted, acknowledged, or scheduled without waiting for the full maintenance timeout.
